title: Regional data bucketing operator playbook
content:
Purpose
This document is a working operator playbook for Regional Data Bucketing — a pragmatic alternative framing to "region pinning" intended for customer onboarding, enforcement modes, and audit evidence collection. It captures operational checklists, enforcement patterns (soft/hard), telemetry hooks, rollback steps, and communication templates. Notes are deliberately operational-first and contain items for follow-up with legal and product.

Scope
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where customers request regional constraints on data storage and inference execution.
- Focuses on per-tenant bucketing by geography (continent/country/region) and per-route exceptions.
- Excludes encryption/KMS design and contractual legal language (see linked artifacts).

Assumptions
- Customer can express residency requirements at onboarding via UI/API: primary_region, allowed_regions, and exception_policy.
- Underlying infra can schedule work to specific region clusters and tag storage buckets with region anchors.
- We have read-only audit log retention for 90 days by default; enterprise customers may require longer.

Key concepts and terminology (operator lens)
- Bucket: logical grouping of customer data and runtime state anchored to a region or set of regions.
- Anchor: immutable tag on a bucket that indicates the 'source of truth' for residency; used for evidence packaging.
- Soft-enforcement: routes requests preferentially to in-region capacity but will fall back to allowed remote regions when capacity exhausted (policy-driven).
- Hard-enforcement: reject or queue requests that cannot be satisfied within the anchored regions.
- Exception: temporary operator-approved override for a tenant/route, recorded with evidence and TTL.

High-level operator workflows
1) Onboarding (sales/CS -> operator handoff)
   - Verify onboarding form includes primary_region, allowed_regions, enforcement_mode, SLA expectations.
   - Run pre-flight checklist: region quotas, capacity reservations, KMS tenancy, VPC peering status (if Private).
   - Create bucket with anchor label, generate evidence bundle template (see evidence section).
   - Kick off a smoke test for read/write and inference TB; log results to the tenant's onboarding ticket.

2) Normal ops (day-to-day)
   - Monitor ResidenceGauge dashboards for cross-region traffic % per tenant and per-route latency anomalies.
   - If cross-region rate > threshold (default 2%) open an incident candidate and annotate tenant record.
   - For soft-enforcement tenants: ensure fallbacks are logged with reason codes and K/V cache rehydration is validated after fallback.

3) Enforcement incident (capacity shortage / misrouting / legal request)
   - Triage: identify whether request is policy, capacity, or misconfiguration. Use "routing-trace:<request_id>" to map path.
   - If misrouting, update routing table and invalidate prefix cache for affected route; push change via routing-config job and monitor.
   - If capacity shortage and tenant is hard-enforced: escalate to Capacity Oncall. Apply temporary traffic shaping (rate-limit remote-region routes) while capacity scales or until customer approves soft fallback.
   - Document all operator actions in the tenant's evidence bundle.

Evidence collection and audit bundle (operator steps)
- Purpose: produce an auditable bundle proving that tenant requests were constrained to the declared regions, and explaining any deviations.
- Minimum evidence items (per-bundle): anchor manifest (bucket metadata + anchor tag), routing traces for sampled requests (ids and route hops), scheduler allocation logs (timestamps, node ids, region labels), CVs for cache rehydration (KV miss/hit rates), operator action log (who, what, why), and customer-facing comms sent.
- Storage: evidence bundles are stored in a write-once audit bucket with TTL based on customer tier. For enterprise, tag with legal-case-id if present.

Enforcement modes — practical guidance
- Soft (default for self-serve): prefer in-region resources; fallback allowed. Operator actions: alert but don’t block; collect traces and notify customer via usage report.
- Hard (enterprise-only, contract-backed): block or queue cross-region requests. Operator actions: pre-reserve capacity, validate autoscaler policies, run canary sims weekly. If fallback is required, request signed exception from customer legal.

Telemetry and alerting knobs (operator cheat sheet)
- ResidenceGauge: per-tenant % of tokens processed outside primary_region (alert threshold 2% / 0.5% for high-security tenants).
- AnchorIntegrity: cron job that validates anchor tags are present on all storage objects (daily). Alert severity: P2.
- RoutingDrift: tracks changes in routing table that cause >1ms added latency in-region.
- EvidenceGap: detects missing pieces in the evidence bundle (e.g., missing scheduler logs) and auto-escalates to SRE.

Testing playbook (pre-deploy and ongoing)
- Staging sim: generate traffic with geo headers and simulate 80% in-region capacity and 20% remote capacity. Validate soft fallback latency and cache correctness.
- Chaos run: run geo-failure test that brings down a regional pool and ensure fallback paths observe SLA and that evidence bundles include failure context.
- Regression tests: nightly run that exercises anchor manifest generation and the evidence-bundle storage pipeline.

Customer communication templates (snippets for SRE/CS)
- Onboarding success: "We created your regional bucket anchored to {primary_region}. Evidence bundle will be available under the tenant record. If you need hard enforcement, reply with contract reference."
- Deviation alert (soft): "We observed {percent}% of recent requests routed outside {primary_region} due to capacity shaping. No data was stored outside allowed regions. See evidence: {link}."
- Enforcement escalation (hard): "A request could not be served within your locked regions and was blocked. To proceed we need a signed exception or we will schedule capacity expansion."

Open questions and unresolved items
- Granularity: should anchors support per-route anchors (some customers want LLM compute in EU but logs in US)? tradeoffs for complexity vs evidence clarity.
- Evidence retention: default 90 days may not satisfy regulated customers — need pricing and S3/Tape options.
- Cross-tenant caching: how to handle shared caches on edge nodes without leaking residency metadata?

Action items (owners and rough ETA)
- Product: define onboarding API fields for "exception_policy" and UI hints (owner: Maya P., ETA: 2026-01-15).
- SRE: implement AnchorIntegrity monitor and EvidenceGap alert (owner: Ethan B., ETA: 2026-02-01).
- Legal: propose standard exception form for hard-enforcement overrides (owner: Lena S., ETA: 2026-01-30).
- Ops: create runbook for evidence bundle packaging and storage (owner: Jordan A., ETA: 2025-11-20).

Notes to self / rough heuristics
- Prefer "anchor" language in comms to avoid legal ambiguity of "pin".
- Keep soft enforcement as the default for velocity; reserve hard enforcement for contract sales.
- Evidence should be digestible: include a one-pager that says "what happened" + raw logs for auditors.

References and links
- See linked artifacts above for design doc and PR. Slack thread: #region-residency (search for thread id: G23-anchors).

Revision history
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Jordan A.).
- 2026-01-09: added telemetry knobs (Ethan B.).
- 2026-03-10: clarified evidence bundle minimum set and added action item ETAs.
